rule: Written before judging, from the form's own definitions. Each form as shown, after the evidence check. Symptom: right when it says, in plain words, what the summary says a driver may notice; wrong when it isn't that (not in the summary, or something only a technician sees); rightly empty when the summary says nothing a driver notices; wrongly empty when it does and the form shows nothing. Fix: right when its kind fits the remedy the summary states; wrong when it doesn't; rightly empty (not stated) when the summary states no remedy; wrongly empty when it does and the form shows not stated. Read one by one by Claude, Oct 13, 2026.
